note: Derived from a real filed return, anonymised — name, EIN, address, officer name and email replaced, figures kept. The second real instance of the 25%-foreign-owned pattern, and the harder one: the return reports no activity at all, which is exactly the case where a preparer concludes there is nothing to report. Form 5472 is triggered by ownership and reportable transactions, not by income, so a nil return does not excuse it. The firm had the return and no books.

planted.what: One foreign person owns 100% of the corporation and Schedule K question 7(c) states that zero Forms 5472 are attached. A 25%-or-more foreign-owned US corporation must file Form 5472 for its reportable transactions with the related party, and for a corporation with no other activity the formation, capital contributions and any amounts paid or advanced by the owner are themselves reportable. A nil return is not a reason not to file: the penalty runs per form per year whether or not any tax was due.

Every federal figure on the return is zero across three years, and the balance sheet is zero at both ends, while Schedule K declares an active trade or business (code 541519, IT consulting and staffing services) and Florida question H gives a location for the corporate books. Either the corporation genuinely had no activity, in which case nothing in the file says so, or activity exists and was not booked. There is no trial balance to test it against, so this cannot be resolved from the face of the return and has to be asked.

Schedule L line 6 other current assets, per Statement #8, opens the year at 100 and is blank at the close, with no distribution, write-off or other movement anywhere on the return: Schedule M-2 shows 0 at both ends and Schedule K question 13 reports zero distributions. An asset that disappears without a corresponding entry is an unexplained tie-out failure.

Form F-7004 carries a due date of 08-03-2026 and a preparation date of 09-02-2026, so the Florida extension was prepared a month after the date it had to be filed by. The preparer's own note 059 warns that a late-filed return with no tax due draws $50 per month to a $300 cap, and that a penalty still accrues for any month past the extension due date. The $50 shown as due is the minimum, not the penalty.
